title: Turning Actions and Qualities into Nouns

sections.content: You know *la subida*, *el aumento*, *la decisión* and *la llegada* from B2 Unit 21: nouns made from verbs. The noun keeps the idea of the verb and drops the doer. This lesson uses the same idea in formal writing, and adds nouns made from adjectives.

sections.title: Why nouns?
sections.content: Why write this way? A noun phrase packs a whole clause into a few words, and it can start a sentence. *Los precios aumentaron, por eso muchas familias protestaron* has two clauses joined by *por eso*. With a noun it becomes one: *Debido al aumento de los precios, muchas familias protestaron.* You know *debido a* from B1 Unit 6. News, reports and essays prefer this compact style; in speech people keep the verbs.

items.spanish: El aumento de los precios preocupa a las familias.
items.english: The rise in prices worries families.

items.spanish: La llegada del presidente se anunció ayer.
items.english: The president's arrival was announced yesterday.

items.spanish: La rapidez del cambio sorprendió a todos.
items.english: The speed of the change surprised everyone.

items.spanish: Debido a la dificultad del examen, muchos estudiantes protestaron.
items.english: Because of the difficulty of the exam, many students protested.

sections.content: Do not pile up nouns joined by *de*: *la decisión de la modificación de la ley* is heavy. One or two *de* are enough. If a phrase gets long, go back to the verb: *se decidió modificar la ley*. Remember the gender comes with the ending: *la* dificultad, *el* aumento.
